title: Tesla Stock (TSLA) Falls 0.2% to $384.68 (Nov 24)
summary: Tesla stock (TSLA) slipped 0.20% to $384.68 on Nov 24 while the Nasdaq fell 1.48%, and the FT reported directors named to steer a SpaceX merger.
body_markdown:
The broader market was mixed. The Nasdaq Composite fell 1.48% to 23,733.54 and the S&P 500 slipped 0.50% to 7,201.09, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 0.85% to 50,018.70. The US 10-year Treasury yield closed the session at 4.91%, down 1.0 basis points. Against the Nasdaq, Tesla's move was 1.28 percentage points better.


Among related names, SpaceX fell 5.65% to $125.81,[Nvidia (NVDA)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/nvda/) dropped 5.86% and electric vehicle maker[Rivian (RIVN)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/rivn/) gained 1.16%. Tesla now sits 22.88% below its 52-week high and 29.36% above its 52-week low.


## Why Tesla Stock Fell


The reports reviewed for this article named no Tesla-specific cause for the 0.20% decline, and[Stocktwits](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/rbc-expects-spacex-tesla-deal-215533238.html) described the stock as closing flat. The move tracked the market instead. Per[Yahoo Finance market coverage](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/live/stock-market-today-tuesday-november-24-dow-sp-500-nasdaq-chip-stocks-nvidia-140629923.html) , tech stocks fell on Tuesday, led by chipmakers, as Nvidia slid after[its Monday surge on Jensen Huang returning as CEO](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/news/nvidia-nvda-stock-news-november-24-2026/) and worries about a December rate hike returned to focus.


The day's Tesla news centered on the possible SpaceX merger. According to[Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/article/tesla-and-spacex-assemble-deal-teams-for-a-merger-that-could-give-musk-majority-control-144555932.html) , the Financial Times reported on Tuesday that the two companies appointed five directors to oversee talks on a potential $3.5 trillion all-stock merger: Robyn Denholm, Kathleen Wilson-Thompson and Jack Hartung from Tesla, and Roelof Botha and Randy Glein from SpaceX.


The report said Morgan Stanley and Goldman Sachs advise SpaceX, Evercore advises Tesla, the exchange ratio has not been agreed, and a deal could be reached before year-end.


The committees behind the talks are on record. As[TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2026/10/20/spacex-and-tesla-boards-form-special-committees-to-review-merger/) reported on October 20, Musk told SpaceX's third-quarter earnings call that both boards had formed special committees of independent directors and that, as a conflicted party, he cannot take part in their discussions. Separately, RBC Capital Markets analyst Ken Herbert said on Tuesday that he now expects a deal announcement by early 2027, earlier than the firm previously expected, according to Stocktwits.


## TSLA Stock Analysis: Supporting Factors and Risks


### Supporting Factors


- Tesla held up better than the market, slipping 0.20% while the Nasdaq Composite fell 1.48%.
- Shares recovered from the session's low, closing $9.18 above it.
- In Musk's view, there is merit in combining the companies, citing cooperation on AI software, robotics and Terafab, a joint chip-manufacturing project, according to TechCrunch.


### Risks


- No deal is agreed. Musk said that assuming a combination is a certainty "would be overstating it," per TechCrunch, and the FT report said the exchange ratio is still open.
- Tesla approval is a high bar: Musk noted a deal would need a 50% vote of all shareholders, not only those who vote.
- Yahoo Finance noted that Musk holds about 20% of Tesla's voting power versus 84% at SpaceX, and could end up with majority voting control of a combined company, depending on terms.
- Chip stocks led Tuesday's Nasdaq decline as December rate hike worries returned, a market backdrop that weighed on large technology names.
